newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan life insurers' head says no voluntary accord.
newsitem.headline: Japan life insurers' head says no voluntary accord.

text.p: Japanese life insurers have made no voluntary agreement with non-life insurance companies about the range of business to conduct before the two sides enter each other's turf from October 1 through subsidiaries, Kenjiro Hata, chairman of the Life Insurance Association of Japan said.

He also said that life insurance companies which set up non-life units have not been asked by the Finance Ministry to voluntarily restrict certain types of non-life insurance business. "We received no administrative guidance (on the non-life insurance business) at all," he told reporters at a regular news conference.

U.S. and Japanese working-level officials met in Tokyo on Wednesday for talks on the insurance dispute, the first discussions since negotiators failed to reach agreement by a July 31 deadline. The dispute centres on U.S. allegations that Japan is reneging on the 1994 pact by moving to open up the so-called third sector niche insurance market before deregulating its primary life and non-life sectors.

Hata said that if Meiji's non-life insurance arm could not sell the third sector niche insurance products, it would hurt earnings at the arm as the third sector business accounted for some 30 percent of non-life insurance companies' income.
